item.title: [LU-17916] Enable folio allocation support on the buffed io read/write path (BIO)
item.description:
When support for folios are added to generic_perform_write() we can enable folio based allocations without re-writing the lustre i/o path to use iomap:

https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-nfs/msg104002.html
Updated patch:
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-fsdevel/20240527163616.1135968-2-hch@lst.de/
Depends on (landed for v6.9):
https://patchwork.kernel.org/project/linux-fsdevel/patch/20240521114939.2541461-1-xu.yang_2@nxp.com/

This is tested for NFS
https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-nfs/msg104003.html

suggesting this alone is enough for a 2x improvement in buffered i/o.

Update lustre to use the folio allocation ie: __filemap_get_folio() instead of the grab_cache_page* family.

Provide a __filemap_get_folio() implementation for compatibility with older kernels.

Assuming no large regressions this should be available in kernel v6.11:
Linux kernel commit: v6.10-rc7-2-g9aac777aaf945
filemap: Convert generic_perform_write() to support large folios

stancheff timday it looks like using in-kernel fscrypt (./configure --enable-crypto=in-kernel is broken now on newer kernels that support folios. I have pushed a debug patch at https://review.whamcloud.com/64942 that forces in-kernel fscrypt, but it managed to build on only a few distros.

Also, I am wondering how Lustre handles folios, and how we ensure they are allocated with only one page per folio. This is important as fscrypt is designed to work with one page per folio, see this discussion:
https://lore.kernel.org/all/20250221224153.GA41579@quark.localdomain/
"any filesystem using fscrypt can't support large folios for now."

crypto should work with struct folio as it is currently.

Large folios are not enabled until LU-19895 where we can enable large folios by setting the flag in the inode mapping what order of folios can be allocated.

The default is 0 so Lustre will only allocate a 0 order folio. The only other way a folio of order other than zero can be seen is with DIO when the user page is almost certainly embedded in a large folio.

Since the bounce folio/page and the DIO page are treated as PAGE_SIZE units there should be no issue with encryption.

When we get to large folios things get a bit more complicated but it is essentially similar ... we just have more working keeping track of the bounce folio since we now may have many bounce folios of order 0 mapping into PAGE_SIZE chunks of a larger folio.
AFAIU our in-Lustre copy of fscrypt would work with large folios. But because of the changes that were made, it breaks compatibility with in-kernel fscrypt.

It looks to me like llcrypt API vs fscrypt API have just drifted quite a bit. So it isn't too surprising that in-kernel is broken in el10 and even a bit in el9.  I did not mark anything not see anything folio specific and nothing that would break the assumption that order 0 folios can be used interchangeably with struct page .

fscrypt in newer kernels have better (limited) support for large folios but work is still done in PAGE_SIZE chunks as far as I understand.

https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/65197 gets things back to compiling and testing for in-kernel, however I think the dummy encryption may need some work (those tests did not run) but I have not spent time yet to track down the root cause.

I will keep in mind that in-kernel crypto ought to be included in general kernel compatibility updates so the API drift gets handled more gracefully.

I pushed a debug patch to force building with in-kernel fscrypt, on top of your patch https://review.whamcloud.com/65197:
https://review.whamcloud.com/64942

Build results show some issues with recent kernels:
https://build.whamcloud.com/job/lustre-reviews/123844/

[Claude] patch https://review.whamcloud.com/69505 ("LU-20896 osc: encrypt direct IO pages at their own file index") adds "always_except LU-17916 66a" to sanity-sec.sh for ZFS, and patch https://review.whamcloud.com/69506 ("LU-20896 llite: transfer ciphertext for O_CIPHERTEXT DIO") extends it to "66a 66c". These tests fail on ZFS because of client races with large folios used for direct IO:

  • folio_trylock() in osc_brw_prep_request() can fail when another RPC holds the lock of the same large folio, and that RPC can unlock it before the folio_test_locked() check in osc_encrypt_pagecache_blocks(), which then returns -EINVAL ("prep_req failed: rc = -22").
  • osc_brw_fini_request() checks page 0 of the folio for a hole instead of the page being read, so a direct read into a THP buffer can skip decryption. This is fixed by patch https://review.whamcloud.com/58097 ("LU-17916 clio: switch to struct folio").

The fix for the trylock race, and the removal of these always_except entries, depends on the LU-17916 patches landing first, so it will be based on them rather than adding more page-based code now.
